title: Invalid ${(...)} string interpolation; use $(...) subexpression
description: PowerShell treats ${...} as a variable-name delimiter, not a subexpression operator. Writing "${($obj.Prop)}" or "text ${($h.ms)}ms" inside a double-quoted string does not evaluate the expression; it raises a parse error or emits literal/garbled text. The correct subexpression operator inside a double-quoted string is $(...). This recurred while formatting engine status output, e.g. "no response (${($h.ms)}ms)" which should be "no response ($($h.ms)ms)".
detection_method: Regex scan for a ${ token immediately followed by ( (optionally whitespace). A variable name can never begin with an open parenthesis, so this sequence is always a misused subexpression.
preventionRule: Inside double-quoted strings, use $(expr) for subexpressions; reserve ${name} strictly for variable names that contain special characters (e.g. ${env:PATH}).
